newsitem.title: POLAND: Early zloty flat in cautious trade, O/N steady.
newsitem.headline: Early zloty flat in cautious trade, O/N steady.

text.p: The Polish zloty remained tied around 2.10 percent from the trading band centre with players bidding cautiously in potentially volatile dollar/mark swings.
Dealers said the dollar's near-term position against major world currencies remained uncertain after the U.S. unit jumped against the yen and mark in Asian trade on Monday.
"All eyes are fixed on the dollar/mark and trade is cautious this morning," said Adam Roeske of Bank Gdanski SA.
At 0855 GMT the zloty was at 2.12/2.09 percent from the parity rate, flat from 2.14/2.07 percent at 0800 GMT and softer from Friday's close at 2.15/2.13 percent.
It was at 2.8240/50 to the dollar, down from Friday's close at 2.8100/05 and at 1.8647/53 to the mark, up from 1.8717/23.

Dealers said the zloty was likely to trade between 2.2 and 1.9 percent from parity in the near-term and some expected large client orders for both currency-buying and selling to go through the market this week.
On the money market overnight rates remained flat at opening levels of 18.90/19.15 percent as banks regained liquidity after last week's monthly tax payments, dealers said.
At 0900 GMT tomorrow/next rates were at 19.00/19.25 percent flat from opening and Friday's close at 19.06/19.19 percent.

At today's one billion zloty primary auction minimum prices were expected to fall by at least one grosz as uninspiring inflation figures and large expected government needs seen boosting yields for the next several auctions, dealers said.
The minimum price of the benchmark 52-week bill seen around 83.49, against last week's 83.50.
Corporate demand for shorter T-bills seen limited by large November tax outflows, dealers said.
